  (d) Procedure followed for Postal Ballot: 
   In compliance with the provisions of 
Sections 108 and 110 and other applicable 
provisions of the Act, Regulation 44 of the 
SEBI Listing Regulations and the applicable 
MCA Circulars, Members can vote only 
through the remote e-voting. Accordingly, 
the Company provided remote e-voting 
facility to all its Members to cast their votes 
electronically and engaged the services of 
CDSL for facilitating the e- voting process.
   In terms of the applicable MCA Circulars, 
the Company sent the Postal Ballot Notices 
in electronic form only to its registered 
shareholders whose e-mail IDs were 
registered/available with the Depository 
Participants (DPs)/Registrars and Share 
Transfer Agents (RTAs) as on the cut-off 
date. Voting rights were reckoned on the 
paid-up value of the shares registered in 
the names of the Members as on the cut-
off date. Members desiring to exercise 
their votes by electronic mode were 
requested to vote before close of business 
hours on the last date of e-Voting. The 
scrutinizer, after the completion of scrutiny, 
submitted his report.
   The consolidated results of the voting 
by postal ballot and e-Voting were then 
announced and the results were also 
displayed at the Registered Office of the 
Company and on the Company’s website 
besides being communicated to BSE 
Limited, National Stock Exchange of India 
Limited and CDSL.

compliances, inter alia, the Shareholding

electronically on BSE’s Listing Centre.
 i. SEBI Complaints Redress System (SCORES): 
The investor complaints are processed in a 
centralized web-based complaints redressal 
system through SCORES. The Action Taken 
Reports are uploaded online by the Company 
for any complaints received on SCORES 
platform, thereby making it convenient for the

 j. Dispute Resolution Mechanism (SMART ODR): 
In order to strengthen the dispute resolution 
mechanism for all disputes between a listed 
company and/or registrars & transfer agents 
and its shareholder(s)/investor(s), SEBI had 
issued a Standard Operating Procedure (‘SOP’) 
vide Circular dated May 30, 2022. As per this 
Circular, shareholder(s)/investor(s) can opt 
for Stock Exchange Arbitration Mechanism for 
resolution of their disputes against the Company 
or its RTA. Further, SEBI vide Circular dated July 
31, 2023 (updated as on December 20, 2023), 
introduced the Online Dispute Resolution 
(ODR) Portal. Through this ODR portal, the 
aggrieved party can initiate the mechanism, 
after exercising the primary options to resolve 
its issue, directly with the Company and through 
the SEBI Complaint Redress System (SCORES) 
platform. The Company has complied with the 
above circulars and the same are available at 
the website of the Company at https:/ /www.
himadri.com/home/invest or_information

general presentation, press release, earning 
releases of the Company and its business on the

  Section 72 of the Act read with Rule 19(1) of

is mainly useful in the case of those holders who 
hold their shares in their own name. Investors 
are advised to avail of this facility to avoid any 
complication in the process of transmission, in 
case of death of the holders. Where more than 
one person holds the securities of a company 
jointly, the joint holders may together nominate, 
in the prescribed manner, any person to whom 
all the rights in the securities shall vest in the 
event of death of all the joint holders.

Our ESG Foundation:Strategy, Purpose & Progress
Himadri Speciality Chemical Limited remains committed 
to responsible growth by embedding sustainability 
into its business model. Our ESG strategy, "Together 
Towards Tomorrow," is designed to drive environmental 
stewardship, social well-being for people/communities, 
continuous value creation for stakeholders, and ethical 
governance. This strategy covers not only internal 
operations but also those of our value chain partners.
Himadri delivers sustainable, value-added solutions that 
address evolving customer needs. This commitment is 
embodied in the Company’s purpose: ‘Excelling while 
innovating’.  Himadri extends beyond carbon chemistry 
to build competencies, perspectives, and partnerships. 
By leveraging its resident expertise and collaborations, 
Himadri is empowered to lead, create economic value, 
protect the environment, and enrich society.
In line with its commitment, the company has embedded 
Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles 
into its operations. As a forward-thinking organization, 
Himadri is shaping the future through strategic sector 
choices, innovative products, efficient processes, and 
responsible practices.
At Himadri, our core philosophy revolves around 
sustainability and responsibility, ensuring both short-
term and long-term value creation. However, the essence 
of our progress is captured in a single, powerful word—
"together."

Glimpse of capex undertaken in FY 24-25 to 
advance environmental stewardship
Reclaiming Waste Heat from Line #3 Secondary APH:
Previously, hot air (around 350°C) from our Line #3 
process was being released into the atmosphere. 
This waste heat stored valuable energy that could 
support our boiler operations. Following energy audit 
recommendations, we installed a duct to redirect this hot 
air into Boiler #3. This reduced the reliance on ambient 
air (~30°C), improving boiler efficiency and reducing fuel 
consumption. Steam generation increased from 69.14 to 
73.86 TPH using the same amount of fuel. The use of hot 
air also replaced diesel during maintenance and lowered 
the power demand of the fans. This initiative saved over 
9,559 MWh of energy annually and cut approximately 
4,588 tons of CO2 emissions.
Smarter Control of Boiler Feed Pumps Using VFDs:
Our boiler feed pump was previously delivering more 
pressure than necessary, leading to energy losses. To 
address this, we implemented an advanced control 
system that adjusts pump speed based on real-time 
demand. Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs) were added 
to fine-tune the pump’s output. This optimization reduced 
the discharge pressure from 81 to 75 kg/cm2, bringing it 
closer to the actual requirement. As a result, the system’s 
energy use decreased by 204 MWh per year, and 98 
tons of CO2 emissions were reduced, enhancing both 
efficiency and environmental performance.
Optimizing CO Pump Pressure with Impeller De-staging:
Some of our CO pumps were producing more pressure 
than required, causing unnecessary energy use and GHG Emission Trend

system wear. Instead of installing electronic controls, we 
applied a mechanical solution: removing two impeller 
stages from the pump. This reduced the discharge 
pressure to a more suitable 35 kg/cm2 and eliminated 
excess recirculation. The change lowered the pump’s 
energy consumption from 109 to 84 kWh, resulting in 
annual energy savings of 213 MWh and a CO2 emissions 
reduction of about 102 tons.
Sealing Leaks in the Compressed Air System:
A detailed survey revealed that 12.5% of our compressed air 
was being lost through undetected leaks. Using ultrasonic 
equipment, we identified and sealed these leaks, reducing 
overall air loss to 9.8%. This action recovered around 202.7 
CMH of compressed air and improved system efficiency. 
The improvement translated into an annual energy saving 
of 177.6 MWh and a reduction of 85 tons of CO2 emissions. 
This simple yet effective measure helped optimize one of 
our most energy-intensive utilities.
Installing Zero-Loss Drains in the Compressed Air 
System:
Earlier our air drainage system operated on a timer, 
releasing compressed air every minute regardless of 
actual need. This led to continuous loss of air and energy. 
We replaced these with zero-loss drains that only activate 
when moisture is present. This upgrade was implemented 
on both the 6-bar and 12-bar compressor lines. Together, 
the systems saved 320 MWh of energy per year and 
reduced 147 tons of CO2 emissions, all through a simple 
automation improvement.
Water Management
Himadri continues to focus on established water 
management initiatives, including monitoring water 
stress levels across relevant sites. Adequate water 
availability for cooling and production processes is 
essential. Himadri implemented regular analyses of short, 
medium and long-term water risks across sites. During 
the reporting period, Himadri widened its water stress 
assessments to encompass a comprehensive evaluation 
of water related risks. Himadri is committed to sustainable 
water management, adopting advanced technologies 
and practices to reduce freshwater consumption, recycle 
wastewater and mitigate environmental impact. 
Water risk analysis and reduction goals: Himadri utilises 
the WRI Aqueduct tool to analyse physical risks such as 
water stress, flooding and water quality. The Company 
conducts water risk assessments based on water basins 
and site-specific water use. With a goal to reduce specific 
freshwater intake by 20% relative to production volume 
between 2021 and 2026, Himadri has implemented 
various measures across its production sites.  All Himadri plants employ Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) technology 
through an Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) integrated 
with a Water Recovery Plant (WRP). This system ensures 
wastewater recycling and efficient reuse, significantly 
reducing groundwater consumption. 
We also aim at enhancing water efficiency, by adhering 
to the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)
with advanced water-saving technologies for improved 
water management. We will align with the National 
Water Mission by monitoring and minimizing water 
withdrawal and consumption. Additionally, the purpose 
of this framework is to outline the procedures and 
responsibilities for monitoring and managing waste water 
quality at Himadri. The objectives are to: 
	 Achieve and exceed Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) 
objectives. 
	 Reduce the intensity of fresh ground water 
withdrawal by 20% by 2026 against baseline (2021). 
	 Reduce daily water consumption by 20% by 2026 
against baseline (2021)
	 Enhance capabilities to recycle and repurpose water 
resources, ensuring a minimal ecological footprint. 
	 Maintain consistent and transparent disclosure 
of advancements to uphold accountability and 
stakeholder trust. Himadri is committed to 
environmental sustainability with Zero Liquid 
Discharge (ZLD) through the comprehensive reuse 
of wastewater from our processes. Our advanced 
Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) and Water Recovery 
Plant (WRP) are pivotal in this endeavor.
As mandated by our comprehensive Water Management 
framework, water audit including water withdrawal, water 
consumption and waste, is to be conducted in every three 
years by engaging independent external third party. 
Additionally, our in house internal auditors regularly 
conduct water withdrawal and consumption review as 
per instructions from Ministry of Jalshakti, Government 
of India. Moreover, water conservation projects and their 
impact is monitored every year by engaging external 
third party and internal team. Water management data 
are subsequently verified by another independent third 
party verifier.
At Himadri, we have implemented an efficient condensate 
recovery system, which enables operation to recover 60% 
of the low-pressure (LP) steam used in all equipment, 
line tracing and coils. Through an efficient vapour trap 
system, we condense water from LP vapour, effectively 
reducing our groundwater usage.

Responsible Consumption
Himadri’s efforts to reduce production waste are guided 
by a principle: Avoid Waste. If avoidance is not possible, 
waste should be recycled or used in energy generation. 
If recycling or energy generation is not feasible, waste 
should be disposed safely. The need to establish high-
level circular economies that support sustainable 
economic growth is increasingly critical. Given the 
planet’s finite resources, rising lifestyle standards and 
growing resources demand on account of a rising global 
population, conventional one-way economic models will 
no longer be able to sustain prosperous lifestyles and 
cultures going ahead. To stimulate economic activity and 
move to a decarbonised society, it will be essential to 
reduce the use of fossil-based plastics while addressing 
a growing demand for plastics. In this context, Himadri 
acknowledges the growing importance of reducing 
plastic consumption and enhancing recycling. In addition 
to plastics and hazardous waste, Himadri’s waste 
management initiatives encompass a wide range of Key 
Performance Indicators (detailed below).
	 Achieve <1% waste to landfill intensity by 2026 
against baseline (2021)
	 Increase the use of non- virgin raw materials sourced 
externally to over 95% in production processes
	 Ensure 100% compliance with regulators
Process optimisation is central to Himadri. This includes 
processing of substance streams and the application of 
the 3R principle (reduce, reuse, recycle) across operational 
sites. Where waste cannot be avoided, the focus is 
on mechanical or thermal reprocessing. At Himadri’s 
sites, various types of recyclable waste — plastics, 
glass, paper, food waste, and wood—are segregated 
and dispatched to external recycling firms approved by 
regional pollution control boards. The Company monitors Water Intensity these firms through audits to ensure their corresponding 
compliance with statutory provisions. Himadri adheres 
to the recommendations of state government waste 
management authorities related to handling hazardous 
wastes like effluent sludge, oil-contaminated gloves, jute 
and soak sand. It employs vendors authorised by the 
pollution control boards. The Company reintroduced 
recycled products as inputs following the end-of-life 
phase of its products. Himadri leverages the benefit of 
integrated production sites and systems for systematic 
waste management. Byproducts from one production 
process are repurposed as raw materials of other 
products, widening the value chain. The Company sources 
raw materials from other sectorial by-products (coal tar 
and carbon black feedstock). In addition to reprocessing, 
waste with high calorific value (substitute fuel) is used 
to produce energy, reducing a reliance on primary fossil 
fuels and moderating Company’s carbon footprint.
In the context of a circular economy, using Anthracene 
oil derived from coal tar as a feedstock for carbon black 
production is an innovative and sustainable approach 
that significantly contributes to resource efficiency and 
environmental sustainability. Coal tar, a by-product of 
coal processing, contains a variety of valuable chemical 
compounds, including Anthracene oil. Traditionally, 
Anthracene oil had Limited scope industrially or got 
disposed of, contributing to environmental pollution. By 
redirecting Anthracene oil into the carbon black production 
process, Himadri is not only creating a valuable industrial 
product but also closing the loop in the life cycle of coal 
tar derivatives, ensuring that fewer resources go to waste. 
Additionally, the circularity of this process is critical for 
minimizing the carbon footprint of the carbon black 
industry. By integrating the use of a by-product into the 
production process, total emission reduction is achieved by 
45% compared to Anthracene Oil disposal and combustion.

Himadri plays a vital role in shaping both environmental

A strong advocate of circularity, Himadri has developed

responsible manufacturing.

1.  Supplier Self-Assessment Questionnaire: The 
sustainable procurement journey begins with a 
Supplier Self-Assessment Questionnaire (SAQ), 
which is designed to assess the supplier’s adherence 
to Himadri’s sustainability expectations. This 
comprehensive questionnaire evaluates a supplier’s 
policies, practices, and performance across key 
sustainability dimensions, including:
	 Environmental management (e.g., emissions, 
waste, water use)
	 Labour and human rights (e.g., fair wages, child 
labour, workplace safety)
	 Business ethics (e.g., anti-bribery, data privacy)
	 Supply chain practices (e.g., subcontracting, 
traceability)
	 Governance and compliance
 The SAQ enables suppliers to reflect on their 
sustainability maturity while providing Himadri 
with valuable insights into potential ESG risks and 
opportunities for improvement.
2.  Third-Party Audit (Online/Offsite): To ensure the 
integrity of the self-assessment process, the SAQ 
is followed by an online or offsite third-party audit. 
These audits are conducted by independent and 
globally recognized verification bodies who assess 
the accuracy of the responses submitted, validate 
documentation, and check compliance with relevant 
laws, industry standards, and Himadri’s Supplier 
Code of Conduct.
3.  Composite Risk Rating and Categorization: Based 
on the findings from both the SAQ and the third-
party audit, Himadri develops a composite risk rating 
for each supplier. This rating categorizes suppliers 
into various risk levels—such as low, medium, or 
high—based on their potential ESG risk exposure. 
The objective is to create a transparent view of the 
supplier landscape and prioritize risk mitigation 
efforts accordingly.
4.  Active Supplier Engagement and Risk Mitigation: 
Himadri takes a proactive and collaborative approach 
to risk mitigation. For suppliers identified as having 
medium or high-risk exposure, the Company initiates 
targeted engagement strategies that include:
	 Capacity building through customized training 
and knowledge-sharing sessions
	 Awareness programs to educate suppliers 
on sustainability expectations, compliance 
requirements, and industry best practices
	 Collaborative action plans, where necessary, 
are co-developed with suppliers to close ESG performance gaps through realistic, time-bound 
improvement measures
	 Monitoring and follow-ups to track progress 
and support continuous improvement
 These efforts are geared towards empowering 
suppliers to enhance their ESG capabilities, align 
with global sustainability goals, and ensure long-
term value creation across the supply chain.
5.  Driving Collective Impact: Himadri views suppliers 
as strategic partners in its sustainability mission. 
By embedding ESG performance into procurement 
decisions and encouraging suppliers to take 
ownership of their sustainability journeys, Himadri 
not only strengthens its own value chain resilience 
but also contributes to broader systemic change.
 Through its Sustainable Procurement Framework, 
Himadri is fostering a responsible sourcing 
ecosystem—one that upholds human rights, 
promotes environmental stewardship, and builds 
long-term partnerships rooted in shared values and 
mutual growth.
 Moreover, we actively monitor evolving sustainability 
trends and engage in meaningful dialogues with 
our suppliers and stakeholders. This proactive 
approach allows us to regularly assess and update 
our procurement policies, ensuring they remain 
relevant and impactful. By embracing continuous 
improvement, we reinforce our commitment 
to maintaining high standards in sustainable

“Integrity, Commitment, Passion, Seamlessness,

At Himadri, sustainability is a shared commitment, deeply 
embedded in the Company’s operations and extended 
across the entire value chain. Embracing a collaborative 
approach, Himadri actively engages with partners 
to minimize environmental impact while delivering 
sustainable solutions. Recognizing that its direct and 
indirect emissions (Scope 1 and Scope 2) contribute to 
the Scope 3 emissions of its customers, the Company 
continuously works to lower its carbon footprint by 
developing low-emission, customer-centric products. 
This integrated approach reflects Himadri’s dedication 
to not only advancing its own environmental goals 
but also supporting the sustainability ambitions of its 
stakeholders.
As part of its customer decarbonization initiatives, Himadri 
has developed low carbon footprint fuel oil (HLSFO) a 
cleaner and more efficient alternative to conventional 
coal tar used for combustion in furnaces at steel plants. 
This innovative solution significantly reduces greenhouse 
gas (GHG) emissions and enhances operational efficiency 
due to its high calorific value. By reducing overall material 
consumption, HLSFO directly contributes to Sustainable 
Development Goal (SDG) 12: Responsible Consumption 
and Production, underscoring Himadri's commitment to 
resource efficiency.
Himadri's Integrated circular business model for the steel 
sector exemplifies its leadership in sustainable industrial 
practices. The Company sources coal tar from steel plants and upgrades it using proprietary technology into 
Coal Tar Pitch, HLSFO, and other high-value by-products. 
Among these, HLSFO is supplied back to the steel plants, 
enabling a closed-loop system that minimizes waste 
and maximizes resource reuse. This model reinforces 
sustainability across the value chain by lowering 
environmental impact, improving material productivity, 
and promoting responsible production.
Through such transformative initiatives, Himadri continues 
to drive measurable environmental progress across its 
operations. By embedding sustainable innovation and a 
customer-focused philosophy at the core of its strategy, 
the Company reaffirms its position as a responsible 
industry leader, committed to long-term value creation 
and environmental stewardship.

sustainable and responsible future, it is driving forward 
a suite of transformative and forward-looking initiatives. 
Strategic projects such as Carbon Capture, Utilization 
and Storage (CCUS), fuel diversification, advanced 
energy management systems, and strong commitments 
to Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DE&I), human rights, 
and STEM education are at the heart of this progress. 
These initiatives not only reflect Himadri’s unwavering 
dedication to environmental and social stewardship but 
also position the Company as a pioneer of purposeful 
growth in the chemical industry.
By embedding sustainability deeper into every aspect of 
its operations, governance, and partnerships, Himadri is 
laying the foundation for long-term value creation—not just for its stakeholders, but also for the communities 
it serves and the planet it depends on. These forward-
thinking projects are designed to enhance operational 
resilience, accelerate the transition to a low-carbon 
economy, and empower people through education, 
equity, and innovation.
Looking ahead, Himadri envisions a future where business 
success and sustainability are inseparable. In collaboration 
with value chain partners, policymakers, and civil society, 
the Company is committed to shaping a resilient, inclusive, 
and regenerative future. With bold action, innovation, 
and purpose, Himadri is not just adapting to change—it is 
leading it, ensuring that progress today secures a better 
tomorrow for all.

VII. Transparency and Disclosures Compliances
 Transparency in Himadri refers to the practice of 
openly sharing information, decisions, processes, 
and policies with stakeholders, including employees, 
customers, shareholders, and the Communities. It 
involves being honest, accountable, and forthcoming 
about the organization's activities and operations. At 
Himadri, addressing grievances as an organization 
involves a structured and proactive approach to 
resolve issues and maintain positive relationships. 
Our Grievance Redressal policy being the backbone 
of transparency, establishes a framework which 
involves:
 1.  Establish Channels for Feedback: Creation of 
multiple channels for expressing grievances, 
such as suggestion boxes, hotlines, online 
forums, or regular town hall meetings. Ensuring 
that these channels are accessible by all 
stakeholders. 2.  Dedicated Grievance Handling Team: 
Designating a team within the organization 
responsible for managing and addressing 
grievances. Provided them with adequate 
training in conflict resolution, communication 
skills, and cultural sensitivity.
 3.  Listen and Empathize: Actively listen to 
the concerns and grievances raised by 
stakeholders. Empathize with their perspectives 
and demonstrate genuine concern for their 
wellbeing. Avoid becoming defensive or 
dismissive of their grievances.
 4.  Document and Analyze Grievances: 
Systematically document all grievances 
received, including details such as the nature 
of the issue, the individuals involved, and any 
supporting evidence. Analyze the grievances 
to identify common themes, root causes, and 
trends.
 5.  Prioritize Grievances: Prioritize grievances 
based on their severity, impact on stakeholder 
and organizational resources available for 
resolution. Focus on addressing high-priority 
grievances promptly to prevent escalation and 
maintain trust with the stakeholder.
 6. Transparent Communication: Communicate 
openly and transparently with the stakeholder 
about the organization’s efforts to address 
grievances. Provide regular updates on the 
status of ongoing investigations, resolutions, 
and any changes implemented as a result of 
stakeholder feedback.
 7. Engage Stakeholders: Engage relevant 
stakeholders in the grievance resolution 
process. Collaborate with these stakeholders to 
gather additional insights, leverage resources, 
and implement effective solutions.
 8.  Implement Solutions: Develop and implement 
solutions to address identified grievances in a 
timely and effective manner.
 9.  Follow-Up and Monitoring: Following up with 
the concerned person after implementing 
solutions to ensure that the grievances have 
been adequately addressed. Monitor the 
effectiveness of implemented solutions and 
be prepared to make adjustments based on 
feedback and changing circumstances.VI. CSR Details

26.  Overview of the entity’s material responsible business conduct issues
 Our Sustainability initiative focuses on addressing the most significant sustainability challenges and opportunities. 
Himadri has restructured its material topics and adopted the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive’s double 
materiality assessment. This methodology prioritizes issues based on their impact on the environment, society and 
Himadri’s business, creating financial risks and opportunities. On one hand, organisations must have an impact 
on people and the environment (inside-out). On the other hand, sustainability-related developments and events 
create (new) risks and opportunities for organisations (outside-in). 10.  Continuous Improvement: Continuously evaluate and improve the organization’s grievance handling processes

Himadri’s ISO certifications are a testament to our 
commitment to globally recognized management 
standards and operational excellence. They signal 
to stakeholders—including banks, investors, and 
customers—that we are a well-structured, reliable, and 
growth-ready organization. Achieving ISO certification 
requires rigorous compliance with defined international 
standards, demonstrating that our processes meet best-
in-class benchmarks for quality and governance.
During the current reporting year, we continued to sustain 
our ISO certifications. The details are described below – 
ISO 9001:2015 certification (Quality)
Himadri operates with a robust ISO 9001:2015 certified 
Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring that its 
products and services consistently meet customer 
and regulatory requirements. The QMS framework 
emphasizes continuous improvement, risk-based 
thinking, and customer satisfaction, which are integral 
to Himadri’s commitment to operational excellence and 
product stewardship.
Through systematic quality audits, process control 
measures, and performance monitoring, the Company 
ensures that each stage of its operations—from raw 
material procurement to final product delivery—adheres 
to stringent quality protocols. The ISO 9001 certification, 
renewed through external validation, underscores 
Himadri’s dedication to delivering safe, reliable, and 
sustainable products aligned with global standards.
ISO 14001:2015 certification (Environment)
The ISO 14001 certification, which focuses on 
Environmental Management Systems (EMS), is 
highly significant for Himadri, especially in terms of 
promoting sustainable practices, ensuring compliance 
with environmental regulations, and improving overall 
operational efficiency. ISO 14001 provides a framework 
for Himadri to manage and reduce its environmental 
impact. By identifying and controlling environmental 
risks, such as emissions, waste, water use, and resource 
consumption, Himadri can improve its environmental 
performance. This includes reducing pollution and 
minimizing the ecological footprint of its operations, 
which is particularly important in the chemical industry 
where processes may involve hazardous materials.
ISO 27001: 2013 certification (Information 
Security)
ISO 27001 is the international standard for information 
security management systems (ISMS). Achieving this 
certification ensures that Himadri has robust security measures in place to protect its sensitive data, whether 
it’s related to intellectual property, financial information, 
customer data, or employee records. This is crucial in 
today’s digital age where data breaches can result in 
significant financial and reputational damage. ISO 27001 
helps identify potential security risks, vulnerabilities, and 
threats to information. By implementing the necessary 
controls and policies, Himadri can mitigate risks and 
reduce the likelihood of security breaches, cyberattacks, 
or data leaks. It ensures that all aspects of the company’s 
information security are addressed in a systematic and 
proactive manner
ISO 37001: 2016 certification (Anti-bribery)
The ISO 37001 certification, which focuses on Anti-
Bribery Management Systems (ABMS), is important 
for Himadri for several reasons, particularly as it relates 
to enhancing corporate integrity, improving ethical 
business practices, and ensuring compliance with anti-
corruption regulations. Here’s why this certification is 
crucial for Himadri. ISO 37001 provides a framework for 
Himadri to prevent, detect, and respond to bribery risks 
within its operations. This is important in industries like 
chemical, where business dealings may involve suppliers, 
contractors, and government agencies, all of which 
could present potential risks for corrupt practices. The 
certification helps establish clear policies and procedures 
to prevent bribery, ensuring the company operates with 
integrity. ISO 37001 helps improve Himadri’s overall 
corporate governance by establishing transparency and 
accountability in its operations.
ISO 45001: 2018 certification (Health & Safety)
The ISO 45001 certification, which is the international 
standard for Occupational Health and Safety (OHS)
management systems, is highly important for Himadri, 
especially in terms of ensuring the well-being of its 
employees, enhancing safety practices, and complying 
with regulatory requirements. ISO 45001 provides a 
framework for identifying, controlling, and minimizing 
health and safety risks in the workplace. For Himadri, 
this means creating a safer working environment for 
employees, which is especially important in the chemical 
industry where workers are exposed to potentially 
hazardous materials and processes. By implementing 
ISO 45001, Himadri ensures that its operations are 
designed to protect the health and well-being of its 
workforce. One of the key benefits of ISO 45001 is its 
focus on accident and illness prevention. By identifying 
hazards and implementing controls to minimize risks, 
Himadri can significantly reduce workplace accidents, 
injuries, and occupational illnesses. This leads to fewer 
disruptions in operations, lower medical costs, and less

ISO 50001: 2018 certification (Energy management)
The ISO 50001 certification, which focuses on Energy 
Management Systems (EnMS), is important for Himadri 
particularly in enhancing energy efficiency, reducing 
costs, and demonstrating environmental responsibility. 
ISO 50001 provides a systematic approach for Himadri to 
monitor, measure, and optimize energy use. By adopting 
this standard, Himadri can identify areas where energy 
consumption can be reduced without compromising 
production. This leads to improved energy efficiency, 
helping the company use energy more effectively across 
its operations. Energy costs often represent a significant 
portion of operational expenses, particularly in energy-
intensive industries like chemical and manufacturing. ISO 
50001 helps Himadri implement energy-saving practices, 
such as optimizing equipment, improving operational 
procedures, and reducing wasteful energy consumption. 
These measures can directly result in cost savings, 
improving the company’s profitability.
IATF 16949: 2016 QMS for Automotive industry
The IATF 16949 certification is highly important for 
Himadri. The company is involved in manufacturing 
or supplying products to the automotive industry or 
any sector that is part of the automotive supply chain. 
Here’s a detailed explanation of why the IATF 16949 
certification. Himadri manufactures products such as 
speciality chemicals, components, or materials used in 
automotive manufacturing (e.g., lubricants, additives, 
coatings, etc.), The IATF 16949 certification is critical. 
Which is specifically designed for the automotive industry 
to ensure that products consistently meet high-quality 
standards and comply with safety, performance, and 
environmental regulations. For Himadri, this certification 
ensures that its products meet the precise specifications 
required by automotive manufacturers. Automotive OEMs 
(Original Equipment Manufacturers) and Tier 1 suppliers 
often require that their suppliers adhere to IATF 16949 
to ensure compliance with global quality standards. 
For Himadri, achieving this certification ensures that 
its manufacturing processes and products meet the 
specific requirements of the automotive industry, which is essential for maintaining existing contracts and securing 
new business opportunities within this sector.
SA8000:2014 certification (Social accountability) 
Achieving this certification demonstrates Himadri’s 
commitment to ethical practices, such as respecting 
labour rights, ensuring a safe work environment, and 
promoting fair wages. This can enhance the company's 
reputation, fostering greater trust with customers, 
investors, and stakeholders. The SA8000 standard 
requires compliance with international labor laws and 
human rights guidelines. For Himadri, this ensures that 
its operations meet recognized ethical standards, which 
is important for reducing legal and reputational risks 
related to labor issues such as child labor, forced labor, 
discrimination, and unsafe working conditions.
ISO 22301:2019 certification (Business Continuity 
Management Systems)- Stage-1
Himadri has successfully completed the Stage 1 audit of 
the Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) 
under ISO 22301, demonstrating its commitment to 
ensuring business resilience and continuity in the face 
of disruptions. The Stage 1 audit involved a thorough 
review of the organization’s preparedness, policies, and 
processes related to business continuity. Himadri is now 
preparing for the Stage 2 audit, scheduled for April 2025, 
which will assess the full implementation and effectiveness 
of the system. This step further strengthens Himadri’s 
ability to maintain operations and recover quickly from 
any unforeseen disruptions, ensuring minimal impact on 
its business activities.
ISO 20400:2017 certification (Sustainable procurement 
practices)
Himadri has adopted the principles of ISO 20400:2017 
– Sustainable Procurement Guidelines to embed

ensures that suppliers align with our values on human 
rights, fair labour, ethical conduct, and environmental 
stewardship. This certification reinforces our dedication 
to building a resilient, inclusive, and accountable value 
chain that supports our Net Zero and human rights goals.

comply legal and financial guidelines, avoiding preferential treatment. Monitoring mechanism are in place to track 
repayment schedules and outstanding balances to maintain financial integrity. 
 At Himadri, inclusiveness is a cornerstone of our business philosophy, extending beyond our operations to 
encompass our entire value chain. We firmly believe that supporting women-led businesses, marginalised and 
vulnerable group led enterprises, Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), and local communities plays 
a crucial role in fostering economic growth, social equity, and sustainable development. While our core raw 
materials—by-products of large-cap industries like steel and oil & gas—cannot be directly sourced from these 
groups due to the specialised nature of their production, we have proactively aligned our procurement strategy 
to prioritise consumables from these groups wherever possible. This approach enables us to balance operational 
requirements with our commitment to inclusive growth.

2. Does the entity have processes in place to avoid/ 
manage conflict of interests involving members of 
the Board? (Yes/No) If Yes, provide details of the 
same. 
 Yes, Himadri has instituted robust governance 
mechanisms to prevent and manage conflicts 
of interest among Board members, ensuring 
transparency, accountability, and ethical integrity in 
decision-making.
 All members of the Board, including Independent 
Directors and Senior Management, are bound by 
a comprehensive Code of Conduct. This code, 
approved and periodically revised by the Board, 
provides explicit guidance on expected ethical 
standards, responsibilities, and protocols for 
disclosing potential or perceived conflicts of interest.
 Key Processes and Safeguards:
 1. Disclosure Obligations:
o Directors are required to avoid situations where 
personal or financial interests may conflict with 
those of the company.
o In cases where such conflicts are unavoidable, 
Directors must formally disclose the matter:
	 For Executives: to their immediate superior.
	 For Directors: directly to the Board.
 2. Board-Level Oversight:
o Disclosed conflicts are addressed and recorded 
in Board meetings.
o Independent Directors play a critical role in 
moderating and arbitrating any potential 
conflict between management and stakeholder 
interests. 3. Professional Integrity Standards:
o Directors are required to act objectively, 
ethically, and in the company’s best interest, 
refraining from actions that could bring personal 
gain at the company’s expense.
o Abuse of position, exploitation of opportunities 
arising from their role, and any form of undue 
influence are strictly prohibited.
 4. Independent Directors' Code:
o Independent Directors are required to uphold 
probity, safeguard stakeholder interests, and 
report any concerns regarding unethical 
behavior or potential conflicts.
o They are expected to remain independent in 
judgment, and report loss of independence, if 
any, to the Board.
 5. Governance Meetings and Evaluations:
o At least one exclusive meeting of Independent 
Directors is held annually to evaluate:
	 The performance of the Board and 
Chairperson.
	 Flow of information from management.
o Directors' performance evaluations are used as 
a basis for re-appointment decisions.
 6. Training and Awareness:
o Directors are encouraged to undertake regular 
updates on governance, compliance, and 
emerging risks, including conflict-of-interest 
management.
 7. Confidentiality and Transparency:
o Directors must maintain confidentiality of 
internal deliberations and corporate information, 
disclosing data only under lawful obligation or 
with proper authorization.
 Through these structured practices, Himadri ensures 
that decisions at the Board level are free from bias, 
rooted in integrity, and aligned with the principles of 
responsible corporate governance. This safeguards 
not only the company’s operations but also the trust 
of investors and other key stakeholders.

  At Himadri, the well-being of workers and employees is not just a responsibility—it is a core principle deeply 
embedded in the company’s values and operational ethos. Recognizing that a healthy, secure, and supported 
workforce is vital for sustainable growth and productivity, Himadri has implemented a comprehensive set of 
welfare measures that holistically address the physical, emotional, and social needs of its people. Himadri’s 
well-being framework rests on several foundational pillars:
	 Health Insurance: Himadri ensures that employees and their families have access to quality healthcare 
services through robust health insurance coverage, offering peace of mind in times of medical need.
	 Accident Insurance: Understanding the inherent risks in industrial operations, Himadri provides accident 
insurance to safeguard workers against unforeseen workplace incidents, ensuring financial protection 
and quick recovery support.
	 Maternity and Paternity Benefits: The company supports its employees through the different phases of 
parenthood by offering maternity and paternity benefits, reinforcing its belief in a family-friendly work 
environment and gender inclusivity.
	 Day-care Facility: To further support working parents, Himadri provides accessible and safe day-
care facilities, enabling employees to balance work commitments with family responsibilities without 
compromise.
	 Occupational and Non-occupational Health and Safety Support: Himadri goes beyond compliance by 
offering a comprehensive occupational health and safety system. Regular health checkups, safety drills, 
and wellness programs form part of a proactive approach to maintaining a safe and healthy workplace.
  Together, these initiatives reflect Himadri’s unwavering dedication to building a supportive and empowering 
workplace. The company’s people-centric policies are not only a testament to its ethical leadership but also 
an engine for long-term success and employee satisfaction.
  At Himadri, the health and well-being of our workforce remain a top priority. The Occupational Health 
Centre (OHC) plays a vital role in promoting a culture of safety, wellness, and proactive healthcare within the 
organization. It serves as a comprehensive hub for various health-related services, ensuring both employees 
and contractors receive the care and attention they need.
  One of the key initiatives includes regular health checkups for contractors, ensuring that those working on-
site are medically fit and monitored periodically. In addition, periodic health checkups for employees are 
conducted systematically to track health trends and take preventive measures.
  To support holistic wellness, the OHC facilitates consultations with physiotherapists for employees who 
require physical rehabilitation or recovery support. Likewise, the services of a dietitian are available for those 
seeking nutritional guidance and lifestyle management, promoting long-term health.

and streamline the R&R programme which enhances employee retention by cultivating a sense of value, reducing 
recruitment and on boarding costs. The Company’s alignment with the Global DEI Alliance provides valuable 
resources and insights to embrace diverse perspectives. This approach leads to higher employee engagement, 
satisfaction and retention. The Company’s Nomination and Remuneration Committee supports the attraction, 
retention and motivation of high-calibre talent.
6. Is there a mechanism available to receive and redress grievances for the following categories of employees and 
worker? If yes, give details of the mechanism in brief.
 Himadri has formalised and widely published its grievance mechanisms, which include a standardised hotline and 
reporting system. Relevant personnel are trained to ensure that all complaints are reviewed and escalated when 
necessary. If a complaint is justified, appropriate measures are promptly taken. Employees can report incidents 
confidentially through a toll-free number, email, or an internal portal. External stakeholders, such as contractors or 
suppliers, are also encouraged to report noncompliance. A team comprising the Chief Human Resources Officer, 
Chief Sustainability Officer and Company Secretary handles complaints with sensitivity and impartiality. Employees 
who report incidents are protected against retaliation, ensuring their safety and confidence in the system. Regular 
audits and feedback loops help identify areas for improvement and maintain a harassment-free environment.

 b. What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non-routine 
basis by the entity?
  Himadri’s occupational health strategy is structured around comprehensive safety initiatives. This encompasses 
risk assessment, standardisation of procedures, workplace health promotion, occupational health training, 
occupational hygiene management, occupational health services, rehabilitation and institutional support 
for work-related injuries / illnesses and audits (internal and external). The focus is on identifying potential 
hazards, assessing risks, establishing safety protocols and supporting wellbeing (physical and mental). Himadri 
emphasises hygiene standards, offers medical support and provides support (rehabilitation and institutional). 
This holistic approach underlines Himadri’s dedication to sustain a safe and healthy work environment. Risk 
assessment is key to occupational health at Himadri, ensuring the identification, evaluation and mitigation of 
workplace health hazards to protect employee safety and well-being. This process begins with identifying 
potential hazards, assessing their likelihood and severity and implementing control measures to reduce risks. 
Himadri’s general risk assessment comprises identifying, capturing and recording occupational health risks.
  Himadri has implemented a comprehensive standard operating procedure (Framework) to manage industrial 
noise effectively, ensuring a safe, compliant and comfortable work environment for all employees. Several 
impactful noise reduction measures have already been implemented. For instance, acoustic hoods have been 
installed in high-noise areas such as the CETP and RC zones. Through continuous noise monitoring and the 
adoption of advanced noise mitigation technologies, the Company strives to reduce its environmental impact 
while supporting a quieter, safer workspace.
  Risk assessment is key to occupational health at Himadri, ensuring the identification, evaluation and mitigation 
of workplace health hazards to protect employee safety and well-being. This process begins with identifying 
potential hazards, assessing their likelihood and severity and implementing control measures to reduce 
risks. Himadri’s general risk assessment comprises identifying, capturing and recording occupational health 
risks. Risks are categorised into high, medium and low levels based on the likelihood of prolonged exposure. 
High and medium risks are reviewed monthly by the senior management in the ESG Council level to ensure 
proactive oversight. Himadri prioritises controls, including elimination, reduction, isolation and exposure 
control. Personal protective equipment is provided at no cost to all employees and contractors, reinforcing 
the Company’s health-conscious environment.

  Non-standard (non-routine) activities-Himadri

12.  Act on Opportunities for Continual Improvement
 Safety is not static; Himadri continually seeks opportunities for enhancement. Through lessons learned, 
benchmarking, and technological innovations, the company strives to elevate its safety performance.
 Himadri is committed to complying with all local, national and international health and safety regulations. Regular 
updates on changes to safety laws are communicated to employees and integrated into the company’s safety 
practices. The company ensures that all safety protocols and practices align with the legal requirements.
 Himadri’s occupational health strategy is structured 
around comprehensive safety initiatives. This 
encompasses risk assessment, standardization 
of procedures, workplace health promotion, 
occupational health training, occupational hygiene 
management, occupational health services, 
rehabilitation and institutional support for work-
related injuries / illnesses and audits (internal and 
external). The focus is on identifying potential 
hazards, assessing risks, establishing safety protocols 
and supporting wellbeing (physical and mental). 
Himadri emphasizes hygiene standards, offers 
medical support and provides support (rehabilitation 
and institutional). This holistic approach underlines 
Himadri’s dedication to sustain a safe and healthy 
work environment. Himadri’s Anti-Discrimination 
and Harassment Policy, outlines our stance against 
discrimination and harassment prohibiting any 
behavior such as verbal abuse, inappropriate jokes, 
unwelcome advances and defines measures for 
ensuring compliance, addressing violations, and 
fostering a safe work environment for all employees.  
 Himadri prioritizes occupational health by 
identifying, evaluating, and mitigating workplace 
health hazards to protect employee safety and well-
being. The process involves identifying potential 
hazards, assessing their likelihood and severity, and 
implementing control measures to reduce risks. Himadri categorizes risks into high, medium, and 
low levels based on prolonged exposure likelihood. 
High and medium risks are reviewed monthly by 
senior management, while controls like elimination, 
reduction, isolation, and exposure control are 
prioritized. Personal protective equipment is 
provided free of charge to all employees and 
contractors.
 Himadri is committed to implementing occupational 
health standards to ensure workplace safety and 
employee well-being. These standards align with 
national and international regulations, and Himadri 
conducts regular risk assessments to identify 
potential workplace health hazards. The company 
prioritizes improvements in areas with the highest 
potential risks. Workplace health programs focus on 
stress management, noise control, and ergonomics, 
enhancing employees' physical and mental health, 
increasing morale, and reducing absenteeism. 
Occupational health services are central to Himadri, 
providing medical support, routine health checks, 
and wellness programs. Regular training and 
education on occupational health ensures staff are 
informed about health and safety standards and 
equipped to handle workplace risks. By implementing 
occupational health standards, Himadri promotes 
a safe, healthy, and supportive workplace, ensuring 
long-term wellbeing and protection from potential 
hazards.

Leadership Indicators
1. Provide the processes for consultation between 
stakeholders and the Board on economic, 
environmental, and social topics or if consultation is 
delegated, how is feedback from such consultations 
provided to the Board.
 ESG priorities in the Company are driven from 
the uppermost level i.e., the Board of Directors. 
The Board provides the strategic oversight and 
has constituted an ESG Committee to provide 
guidance and monitor the ESG progress. The ESG 
Committee of the Board has delegated the process 
of undertaking consultations with stakeholders to 
the management. Feedback from such consultations 
is shared with the Committee and the Board. 
Himadri has undertaken a comprehensive materiality 
assessment and stakeholder engagement exercise to identify Environmental, Social and Governance 
(ESG) topics of significance. As a part of this 
exercise, Himadri along with an external agency, 
with requisite experience, engaged with the key 
internal and external stakeholders to understand 
their concerns and incorporate their views into 
materiality assessment, for prioritizing ESG topics 
and frameworks. Insights gathered through 
stakeholder engagement were analysed to develop 
the materiality matrix and arrive at the final list of 
ESG focus areas. The result of this assessment was 
presented to the ESG Committee and the Board. 
The outcome is being considered for defining ESG 
objectives of the Company.

Principle 5
Businesses should respect and promote human rights
SDGs Impacted Businesses must operate in a manner that respects and upholds 
the inherent rights and entitlement of individuals without any 
discrimination. The core tenets of this principle are based on the 
Constitution of India and international Human Rights standards 
such as the International Bill of Rights and UN Guiding Principles on 
Business and Human Rights. 
Equal human right is a fundamental aspect of the Company’s business 
ethics and operational framework, which encompasses its policies, 
processes and practices. The Company’s commitment and respect for 
human rights is translated in its publicly accessible policies, including 
‘Labour and Human rights policy, ‘Code of Conduct’. For Himadri, "dignity 
at work" is not just a commitment but a way of business conduct.

4. Do you have a focal point (Individual/ Committee) 
responsible for addressing human rights impacts 
or issues caused or contributed to by the business? 
(Yes/No)
 Yes, Himadri is committed to fostering a work 
environment grounded in respect, dignity, and 
fairness. In alignment with this ethos, the Company 
has established a robust Whistle Blower and 
Human Rights Grievance Mechanism that serves 
as a focal point for addressing concerns, including 
those related to human rights violations caused or 
contributed to by the business.
 The Company encourages an open-door policy, 
promoting transparency and accessibility across all 
levels. Employees and associates are empowered to 
raise grievances or report any form of misconduct, 
without fear of retaliation, through multiple safe 
channels.
 Key Features of the Mechanism:
	 Reporting Channels: Employees and associates 
may report grievances or violations to the 
Human Resource department or Senior 
Management. The Company strictly prohibits 
any form of reprisal or retaliatory action against 
individuals raising concerns in good faith.
	 Investigation and Redressal: Where necessary, 
a dedicated investigation committee is formed 
to evaluate reported violations. In collaboration with Senior Management, the committee 
ensures prompt resolution and implements 
appropriate remedial actions.
	 Human Rights Due Diligence: The Company 
periodically conducts human rights due 
diligence, monitoring the effectiveness of its 
policies and identifying potential areas for 
improvement in its governance framework.
	 Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH): 
Himadri has a clearly defined POSH Policy 
to prevent and address any form of sexual 
harassment at the workplace. Concerns under 
this category can also be reported through the 
established grievance mechanisms.
5. Describe the internal mechanisms in place to redress 
grievances related to human rights issues.
 In this regard the Company encourages an open-door 
policy. The Company has built a strong mechanism 
for reporting matters or concerns faced at the 
workplace. Himadri recognises the importance that 
business can play in ensuring long term protection 
of human rights and for this reason the company 
is dedicated to upholding the human rights of its 
employees, communities.
 The mechanism is outlined below:
 1.  The employees/ associates can address their 
complaints or grievances or report instances 
to the Human Resource department/ Senior 
Management. No reprisal or retaliatory action 
is taken against any employee/ associates for 
raising concerns under this policy.
 2.  If the situation warrants, a committee is formed 
to investigate the violations reported. The 
Committee evaluates the violations reported 
and ensures that the same are addressed and 
resolved at the earliest. The Committee also, 
in consultation with the Senior Management, 
provides a suitable remedy.
 3.  The Company periodically undertakes human 
rights due diligence process for management 
and oversight/ monitoring of the policy and 
identifies any shortcomings.
 4.  The Company also has a Policy on Prevention 
of Sexual Harassment (POSH), and any such 
concern can be reported.

Whistleblowing can be used when individuals, such as directors, employees, 
or any other stakeholders, have genuine concerns or grievances related to 
the following issues: 
Unethical behaviour : 
Reporting any action that goes against ethical standar ds or the code of conduct of the company. 
Fraud : 
Reporting actual or suspected fraudulent activities within the organization. 
Violation of the Code of Conduct or Policy: 
Reporting any breaches of the company's code of conduct or policy. 
Breach of business integrity and ethics : 
Reporting actions that compromise business integrity or ethical practices. 
Intentional financial irregularities : 
Reporting instances of intentional financial mismanagement, including fraud. 
Deliberate violation of laws/regulations : 
Reporting actions that violate laws or regulations. 
Gross or willful negligence causing danger : 
Reporting actions that pose substantial and specific danger to health, safety, and the environment. 
Manipulation of company data/records : 
Reporting any attempts to manipulate or falsify company data or records. 
Pilferage of confidential/propr ietary information: 
Reporting unauthorized access or use of confidential company information. 
Gross wastage/misappropriation of company funds/assets : 
Reporting instances of significant misuse or misap prop riation of company funds or assets.

 Himadri actively fosters a workplace culture where diversity is embraced, and inclusivity is woven into everyday 
operations. Employees are encouraged to engage in meaningful dialogue that promotes empathy, understanding, 
and mutual respect—strengthening the social fabric of the organization.
 In line with its commitment to human rights and ethical conduct, Himadri has established a strong Prevention of 
Sexual Harassment (POSH) Policy. The policy enforces a zero-tolerance approach to harassment and is aligned with 
national legal frameworks. It aims to create a safe, respectful, and inclusive work environment for all employees.
 To ensure robust implementation, an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) is in place, functioning with complete 
confidentiality and impartiality. The ICC not only addresses reported incidents but also conducts awareness 
sessions and regular training to help employees identify and prevent harassment. These efforts are integral to 
building a workplace rooted in accountability, dignity, and psychological safety.
 Himadri’s proactive stance on POSH and inclusive culture reflects its broader commitment to employee well-being, 
social equity, and sustainable corporate responsibility.

 Himadri employs a multifaceted approach to reduce 
water withdrawals, integrating Rainwater Harvesting, 
Steam Condensation, Water Recovery through Water 
Recovery Plants (WRP), and Zero Liquid Discharge 
(ZLD) capacity expansion. We are committed in 
reducing daily water consumption by 20% within 
2026. Our Water Efficiency and Preservation 
Policy upholds our integrity towards delivering to 
a sustainable world. The pursuit of water positivity 
through a zero liquid discharge (ZLD) process helps 
moderate environment impact and enhance water 
resource sustainability. Our initiatives align with 
UNSDG 6 (Clean water and sanitation). 
 In the fiscal year 2024-25,we achieved a significant 
reduction in our average daily water consumption 
which is a daily savings of 462KL
 To accomplish this, we implemented several key 
initiatives:
 • Arresting Steam Leakages: We focused on 
arresting steam leakages in the Captive 
Power Plant (CPP) and Central Boiler Division 
areas. This helped in reducing water loss and 
improving overall efficiency.
 • Condenser Recovery System: We installed a 
condenser recovery system in the CPP, which 
allowed us to recover and reuse water that 
would otherwise be lost.
 • Heat Exchanger in Blowdown Line: By 
integrating a heat exchanger in the blow down 
line of the CPP, we were able to recover heat and 
reduce water consumption for other processes.
 • Minimizing Intermittent Blowdown (IBD) and 
Continuous Blowdown (CBD): We minimized 
the IBD (procedure to remove suspended 
solids, including any sludge formed in the 
boiler water) and CBD (continuous removal of a 
small amount of water from the boiler, typically 
from the surface, to control the concentration 
of Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) and maintain 
boiler water quality processes in the CPP as per 
water quality analysis, further reducing water 
wastage. • Water Recovery System: We implemented a 
comprehensive water recovery system (New 
Water Recovery Plant) to reclaim and reuse 
water within our operations.
 • Fill Pack Replacement: We replaced the fill 
pack in our cooling towers, which improved the 
efficiency of our cooling processes and reduced 
water usage.

5. Has the entity implemented a mechanism for Zero 
Liquid Discharge (ZLD)? If yes, provide details of its 
coverage and implementation
 Yes, to support our wastewater recycling and Zero 
Liquid Discharge (ZLD) system, Himadri has established 
an advanced Water Recovery Plant (WRP)—the final 
recovery stage of our Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP). 
This innovative system is designed to maximize water 
reuse, minimize waste, and significantly reduce our 
reliance on freshwater resources.
 The WRP receives treated wastewater from various 
sources, including the ETP, DM plant backwash, RO 
plant reject water, and cooling tower blowdown. 
These are collected in the WRP feed tank and 
then directed to a clarifier, where a carefully dosed combination of dolomite, polyelectrolyte, sodium 
hypochlorite, caustic, and coagulant helps settle 
Total Suspended Solids. The clarified, TSS-free water 
is then stored in a dedicated tank.
 From here, the water undergoes several advanced 
filtration processes:
	 It is first passed through a Mixed Gravel Filter 
(MGF) with Hydrochloric Acid HCL dosing to 
eliminate any residual suspended solids.
	 Next, it enters an Ultrafiltration (UF) unit, which 
separates permeate and reject water into 
respective tanks.
	 The permeate water is then treated through a 
two-stage Reverse Osmosis (RO) system—first 
stage with five membranes, second stage with 
two—after pre-treatment using a carbon filter 
and dosing with HCL, sodium metabisulphite, 
and anti-scalant.
	 Before reaching the final permeate tank, the 
water passes through a De-Gasifier unit to 
remove excess carbon dioxide, ensuring stable 
pH levels.
 Fig: ZLD process
 The final permeate water, with a daily recovery of 
1200 KL, is effectively reused for cooling tower 
makeup, process requirements, and RO plant feed. 
Meanwhile, the final concentrate water amounting 
to 50 KL per day, is sustainably utilized in various 
places of our manufacturing unit. This integrated 
system showcases Himadri’s commitment to 
responsible water management by significantly 
reducing groundwater consumption and reinforcing 
our vision for sustainable industrial operations.Process water

	 The Vehicle Management Standard 
(Framework) implemented by Himadri plays a 
vital role in reducing air pollution. By ensuring 
that all vehicles within the plant premises are 
roadworthy and fully compliant with local 
regulations, particularly those governing the

minimizes the emission of harmful pollutants.

with a robust preventative maintenance system,

in lower pollutant emissions. The Framework 
also mandates strict adherence to speed limits 
and prohibits the use of mobile phones while 
driving, reducing the risk of accidents and 
unnecessary idling, both of which can contribute 
to air pollution. By maintaining vehicles in 
optimal condition and enforcing stringent 
operational protocols, Himadri significantly 
reduces pollutant emissions, supporting cleaner 
air and demonstrating its commitment to 
sustainability and environmental stewardship.
	 The Hot Material Vapour Scrubbing Unit is 
designed to remove certain components from 
gases or vapours by washing them with a liquid 
absorbent called wash oil. The liquid, enriched 
with absorbed constituents, is then replaced 
with fresh liquid. The scrubber unit uses a 
packed tower where the gas enters from the 
bottom and the scrubbing liquid enters from the 
top, leading to absorption and condensation of 
vapors. To maintain the liquid temperature, a 
cooling coil with circulating water is employed. 
The unit follows a daily checklist, monitoring the 
level and temperature of the scrubbing liquid. 
If the temperature exceeds the limit, the water 
inlet valve is adjusted.   Additionally, the cloud point of the liquid is 
tested, and if it goes beyond the specified 
temperature, the liquid is replaced. The optimal 
level range of the scrubbing liquid is 40% 
to 60%, with a temperature range of 45°C to 
55°C and a cloud point of 35°C. To control 
vapour emissions from light oil tanks, a nitrogen 
blanketing system is installed, reducing air 
pollution. The nitrogen pressure is regulated to 
maintain controlled pressure inside the tank. If 
the pressure increases, the tank vent actuator 
releases the excess pressure to the atmosphere. 
On the other hand, if the pressure decreases, the 
nitrogen actuator opens to introduce nitrogen 
and maintain the set tank pressure. 
	 The presence of nitrogen in the tank reduces 
air pollution by exhausting nitrogen first during 
vapour release, leading to the condensation of 
light oil vapour into liquid inside the tank. The 
NOx Abatement Process at Himadri aims to 
reduce NOx emissions from the cellulose nitration 
reactors at the site. The process consists of two 
main components: a scrubber/absorber tower 
and a reaction vessel with a catalyst bed. The 
scrubber/absorber tower comes in contact with 
NOx-laden fumes with water, producing nitric 
acid through absorption. Moreover, we regularly 
monitor POP across all our plants.
Note: Indicate if any independent assessment/ 
evaluation/assurance has been carried out by an 
external agency? (Y/N) If yes, name of the external 
agency.
 Yes, Himadri undertakes thorough and regular 
evaluations of major air pollutants to ensure 
adherence to environmental standards and to protect 
public health. Third-party experts are engaged

supports Himadri’s commitment to environmental

10. Briefly describe the waste management practices 
adopted in your establishments. Describe the 
strategy adopted by your company to reduce usage 
of hazardous and toxic chemicals in your products 
and processes and the practices adopted to manage

Himadri’s efforts to reduce production waste are 
guided by a principle: avoid waste. If avoidance is 
not possible, waste should be recycled or used in 
energy generation. If recycling or energy generation 
is not feasible, waste should be disposed safely. The 
need to establish high-level circular economies that 
support sustainable economic growth is increasingly critical. Given the planet’s finite resources, rising 
lifestyle standards and growing resources demand on 
account of a rising global population, conventional 
one-way economic models will no longer be able 
to sustain prosperous lifestyles and cultures going 
ahead. To stimulate economic activity and move to 
a decarbonised society, it will be essential to reduce 
the use of fossil-based plastics while addressing 
a growing demand for plastics. In this context, 
Himadri acknowledges the growing importance 
of reducing plastic consumption and enhancing 
recycling. As a speciality chemical manufacturing 
Company, Himadri takes a comprehensive approach 
to identify risks associated with various types of 
waste, including production waste, packaging waste, 
plastics and wood pallets. The Company considers 
a range of plausible scenarios through consultations 
with internal and external stakeholders.
 Process optimisation is central to Himadri. This 
includes in-plant reprocessing of substance 
streams and the application of the 3R principle 
(reduce, reuse, recycle) across operational sites. 
Where waste cannot be avoided, the focus is on 
mechanical or thermal reprocessing. At Himadri’s 
sites, various types of recyclable waste — plastics, 
glass, paper, food waste and wood—are segregated 
and dispatched to external recycling firms approved 
by regional pollution control boards. The Company 
monitors these firms through audits to ensure their 
corresponding compliance with statutory provisions.
 Himadri adheres to the recommendations of state 
government waste management authorities related 
to handling hazardous wastes like effluent sludge, 
oil-contaminated gloves, jute and soak sand. It 
employs vendors authorised by the pollution 
control boards. The Company reintroduced recycled 
products as inputs following the end-of-life phase 
of its products. Himadri launched a pilot project to 
implement a reusable packaging solution, with the 
potential to eliminate plastics and wood from its 
packaging.
 Besides, the Company strives to achieve its 
ambitious waste management target (zero waste to 
landfill). Himadri leverages the benefit of integrated 
production sites and systems for systematic waste 
management. By-products from one production 
process are repurposed as raw materials of other 
products, widening the value chain. The Company 
sources raw materials from other sectorial by-
products (coal tar and carbon black feedstock). In 
addition to reprocessing, waste with high calorific 
value (substitute fuel) is used to produce energy, 
reducing a reliance on primary fossil fuels and 
moderating Company’s carbon footprint. Himadri 
is exploring alternatives to replace virgin materials.

 Himadri has strengthened its climate action framework by formally including Scope 3 emissions in its greenhouse 
gas (GHG) accounting and disclosure process starting FY 2023–24. Recognising that a significant portion of its 
total emissions lies beyond its direct operations, this strategic inclusion marks a key milestone in Himadri’s journey 
towards comprehensive climate responsibility and alignment with global best practices.
 The Company has undertaken a structured approach to Scope 3 management, beginning with detailed mapping 
of its value chain to identify hotspots and high-emission categories. Priority areas such as purchased goods and 
service, upstream transportation, and downstream transportation have been brought under focus for accurate 
data collection and emissions quantification. 
 To drive meaningful impact, Himadri has set an ambitious yet achievable Scope 3 emission intensity reduction 
target of 5% by 2025, compared to its 2023 baseline. This target is aligned with the Science Based Targets initiative 
(SBTi) and supports the broader global goal of limiting temperature rise to below 1.5°C. It also reflects Himadri’s 
commitment to responsible growth by embedding sustainability deeper into its value chain.
 Previously, industry average data were used to account Himadri’s Scope-3 emission. However, with the direction of 
our BoD members in this current year we embarked on a journey to enhance the granularity of data for a detailed 
emission profile. Therefore, praxis of data collection had been modified accordingly and Himadri launched a formal 
value chain engagement process. 
 To ensure that sustainability is ingrained throughout our supply chain, Himadri employs a multi-stage process 
for evaluating Value Chain Partners. Each Value Chain Partner is required to complete a detailed self-assessment 
survey that covers ESG and other business aspects. Depending on the risk profile of each Value Chain Partner, we 
conduct either on-site or remote audits. These audits focus on key areas of performance, including environmental 
management, health and safety protocols, labor practices, and corporate governance. Then each Value Chain 
Partner is categorised on respective risk indexes and then corrective action plans are shared with the partners to 
mitigate any potential risk. As a environmentally conscious organisation Himadri takes a pro-active collaborative 
approach to carry out any environmental stewardship projects. One such initiative includes the planned shift from 
conventional diesel to biodiesel for both upstream and downstream logistics — a move that not only reduces 
emissions but also supports India’s national biofuel mission.  
 By adopting this forward-looking and collaborative approach, Himadri is not only strengthening its Scope 3 
inventory but also fostering innovation and shared responsibility across the value chain. These efforts underline 
Himadri’s vision to lead by example in building a low-carbon, resilient and sustainable future for all stakeholders.
Note: Indicate if any independent assessment/evaluation/assurance has been carried out by an external agency? 
(Y/N) if yes, name of the external agency.
Yes, we have employed an independent third party to account our GHG emission. This particular assessment was 
carried out by TUV SUD South Asia Pvt Ltd. during the current reporting year. Accounting is done in accordance 
of methodologies detailed by Green House Gas Protocol which is a global standard.

7 Environmental

: 480 TPD Project 
–New RC-Coal Tar 
DivisionHimadri has implemented a strategic 
approach to energy reduction by transitioning 
from a single-stage cooling system (Old RC) 
to an advanced double-stage cooling system 
(New RC). In the previous system, the total 
heat load was forwarded directly to the 
cooling tower, leading to higher energy and 
water consumption. With the New RC system, 
the total heat load is divided into two streams: 
one directed towards RO (Reverse Osmosis) 
water and the other towards the cooling 
tower.This division significantly reduces 
the heat load on the cooling tower, 
resulting in lower evaporation 
losses—saving approximately 8 KL 
of water per day. Additionally, the 
New RC system improves energy 
efficiency by converting excess 
heat into steam, which is forwarded 
to the LP steam header for reuse.
5. Does the entity have a business continuity and disaster management plan? Give details in 100 words/ web link.
 Himadri has developed a robust Business Continuity and Disaster Management Plan (BCDMP), which is integrated 
into the Company’s comprehensive Risk Management Policy. This forward-thinking plan is a testament to Himadri’s 
unwavering commitment to operational resilience, long-term value creation, and sustainable business growth, even 
in the face of unforeseen disruptions. Himadri has successfully conducted the Stage 1 audit for ISO 22301:2018, the 
international standard for Business Continuity Management Systems (BCMS). This audit marks a significant step in 
Himadri's commitment to ensuring the resilience and continuity of its operations.
 The BCDMP serves as a strategic blueprint to ensure uninterrupted operations during natural calamities, industrial 
emergencies, cyber threats, and other potential disruptions. It reflects Himadri’s focus on protecting stakeholder 
value, enhancing corporate governance, and aligning with its long-term strategic objectives. The plan outlines 
procedures to maintain critical business functions, secure employee and community safety, and preserve 
environmental integrity—minimizing harm to people, infrastructure, biodiversity, and ecosystems.
 Himadri’s approach to risk management is proactive and data-driven. All financial and non-financial risks are 
continuously identified, assessed, and mitigated under the guidance of the Risk Management Committee, 
a dedicated oversight body that reports directly to the Board. This includes climate-related risks, operational 
disruptions, supply chain vulnerabilities, and emerging ESG concerns.
 To ensure that the BCDMP remains dynamic and effective, regular simulations, risk assessments, and audits are 
conducted. These evaluations help identify gaps, incorporate learnings, and update response protocols in line with 
evolving business environments and global best practices. Employees across critical functions are also trained to 
respond efficiently during emergencies, reinforcing a culture of preparedness and accountability.
 Through this integrated and forward-looking risk governance framework, Himadri not only safeguards its assets 
and people but also ensures that it continues to deliver value to customers and communities—even in times of 
crisis. This resilience is fundamental to Himadri’s sustainable growth vision and its ability to thrive in an increasingly 
complex and interconnected world.

There were no incidents of anti-competitive behaviour involving the Company during the reporting period 
(2024-25).2. Provide details of corrective action taken or underway on any issues related to anti-competitive conduct by the 
entity, based on adverse orders from regulatory authorities.
 Himadri’s fair competition policy ensures a compliance with anti-trust laws and promotes fair trade in accordance 
with guideline provided by Competition Commission of India. Employees are trained to recognise and avoid 
practices like price fixing or monopolistic behaviour. To detect non-compliance, the Company established strong 
vigilance mechanism and reporting channels that employees, personnel from staffing agencies working at its 
premises and external stakeholders to report compliance violations. We conduct frequent legal and ethical reviews, 
involving internal and external legal advisors. We implemented strict internal controls to detect and prevent any 
potential anti-competitive behaviour. All these measures helped us to achieve zero incidents of anti-competitive 
behaviour consistently.
 Additionally, our Grievance Redressal policy which is publicly available, establishes an anonymous complain 
channel for all the stakeholders. Any stakeholder can reach us via any means such as email, phone call, or any 
such established mechanism. Anonymity of the complainant is ensured through the highest authority level of 
the company. Company Secretary, Chief Sustainability Officer, and Chief Human Resource Officer are part of the 
committee to oversee the grievances, its effective Redressal, and overall efficacy of our established mechanism.

or agent details, and any supporting images. The complaint is immediately shared with the Head of Technical 
Services and the Head of Quality Control. Customers receive an acknowledgment from the Regional Marketing 
Manager, assuring them that their concern is being acted upon.
 Within one working day, the Head of Technical Services forwards the complaint internally to the relevant department 
heads. These teams collect the necessary data and present their findings in a Corrective and Preventive Action 
(CAPA) meeting within two working days. Appropriate corrective steps are then initiated to resolve the issue. Once 
resolved, the outcome is communicated to the customer by the Marketing Manager. In cases where the complaint 
is found to be unjustified, the Head of Technical Services and Regional Marketing Manager engage directly with 
the customer to provide clarification and close the matter amicably.
 The complaint closure form is completed by the Head of Technical Services and authorized by the Plant Head. If 
the resolution identifies any need for process improvements, necessary updates are made to procedures, work
